prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view of the camera wearer seated on the floor, with their brightly lit lower torso/lap at the bottom center (about 0.2–0.3 m from the camera) and both forearms and hands reaching forward (0.4–0.6 m away) toward a round rolling board on a newspaper-covered floor roughly 0.6–0.8 m below. Within arm's reach, a wooden rolling pin extends forward in the left hand (frames 1–2) or across the board (frames 3–5), a small flour cup sits immediately to the board's left (~0.15 m from the board), a metal plate/bowl sits at the upper right (~0.2–0.3 m from the board), and a tall red cylindrical container stands on the left (~0.5–0.7 m from the camera); no other people are present, though in frame 5 a pan edge enters at the middle right. Across frames 1 to 5, the right hand lifts closer to the camera in frame 2 (~0.35 m), both hands move onto the board to roll dough in frames 3–4, and in frame 5 the camera turns slightly up and to the right, revealing a second plate with dough balls (~0.8 m away) and distant containers on the upper left (~1.0 m away). Compared to the dark, motion-blurred RGB strip, the depth map clearly separates the vertical height of the tall left-side container and the raised rolling pin in frames 1–2 from the flat floor plane. However, the map is unreliable on the shadowy left side of frames 1–3 where green bottles are assigned anomalously far (black) depths, in frame 4 where motion blur flattens the hands and board into an indistinct smudge, and on the flat round board in frame 3 which appears artificially bulged.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map detects only a sparse subset of the workspace across the 5 frames: the camera wearer's lower body/lap at the bottom center in frames 1 and 3 (`person`, ~0.2–0.3 m from the camera), the partly cut-off metal dish at the upper right of frames 1–3 (`bowl` or `cup`, ~0.6–0.7 m away and ~0.2 m above-right of the rolling board), and the round wooden rolling board in the center of frames 2 and 3 (misclassified as `donut`, ~0.6–0.7 m away, directly above the wearer's lap in image space). No other people are in the scene, and all detected regions lie within the camera wearer's immediate arm's reach on the floor directly in front of them, though their hands and forearms occasionally overlap the board's right edge in frame 2. Across the sequence, detections flicker in and out as the hands move and the camera shifts, completely dropping all objects during the motion blur of frame 4 and covering the entire frame 5 with a single false `cake` mask when the camera pans slightly right. While the crisp mask boundaries in frames 2 and 3 help isolate the circular footprint of the rolling board and the upper-right dish against the low-contrast newspaper and floor, the map is highly unreliable overall: it misses the wearer's hands, the rolling pin, the small flour bowl, the left-side containers, and all individual items in frames 4 and 5, while severely misclassifying the wooden board as a donut and the whole fifth frame as a cake.
descriptions.pose: The pose map contains no yellow body skeletons—as no other people are in view and the camera wearer's head and shoulders are behind the lens—and detects only a single magenta left-hand skeleton in frame 2 at the lower-left of the rolling board (~0.5 m from the camera wearer). In that second frame, the detected left hand is positioned just above the camera wearer's lap and to the left of the right hand (~0.25 m apart), gripping the lower handle of the rolling pin within immediate reach of the small flour cup and wooden board. Because the camera wearer is viewed top-down from their own head-mounted camera, their hands extend away from the body toward the floor below, with the rolling pin partially occluding the fingers of the left hand. Although this single detection in frame 2 pinpoints the articulated finger and wrist joints of the left hand gripping the pin in a dim region of the RGB image, the pose map is largely unreliable across the strip: it completely misses the right hand in all five frames and fails to track the left hand in frames 1, 3, 4, and 5 due to dim lighting, downward foreshortening, and motion blur.
